fields.title: Three Places and Three Meanings
fields.keyTakeaway: Encryption in transit protects against interception, at rest protects against media theft, and neither protects against compromised access to a running system.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: "Your data is securely encrypted" — what does this actually mean?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: This phrase is used in marketing more often than it is understood. A promise that does not match reality is a reputational and legal risk, while underestimating what is already there leads to extra work.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: **[[encryption-in-transit|Encryption in transit]]** means data is protected during transmission. Provided by [[tls|TLS]]. Protects against network interception. Today it is mandatory everywhere and is not an advantage.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **[[encryption-at-rest|Encryption at rest]]** means data is encrypted in storage. Protects against physical access to disks and backup leaks. **Does not protect** against someone who has access to the running system: the application reads the data decrypted.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: The latter is the main misunderstanding. Encryption at rest helps almost not at all in a typical leak via compromised access to the application or database.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **[[end-to-end-encryption|End-to-end encryption]]** means data is readable only by the sender and recipient; the service cannot see it. Maximum protection and maximum limitations: you cannot search, you cannot process, you cannot recover if the key is lost. Applicable to messaging, not applicable to a product catalog.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: Separately — **passwords are not encrypted, they are [[hashing|hashed]]** with a [[salt|salt]]. Irreversible transformation: you can verify a match, but you cannot recover the password. If a service is able to send you your password, it is storing it incorrectly.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Everything in transit — TLS, mandatory. Everything at rest — provider-side encryption, enabled by default, costs zero.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: End-to-end encryption is absent and not needed: the product by nature processes data — searches for items, calculates totals, generates reports.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: The wording for users was rewritten twice. The first version promised "full encryption of your data" — the lawyer rejected it as misleading. The final version states specifically: transmission is protected, storage is encrypted, employee access is restricted and logged.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Separately: card numbers are not stored at all — only a token from the payment provider. This is more reliable than any encryption because the data does not exist.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Finally — a general principle repeated across the entire field: **the best data protection is its absence.**
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Encryption at rest may be a regulator requirement regardless of its actual utility. In that case, it is done for compliance, which is a normal reason.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Encryption in transit protects against interception, at rest protects against media theft, and neither protects against compromised access to a running system.
